# Objective
This document reports on the **taxonomic assignment and decontamination** for the Tri5-Mutant-Microbiome project on wheat heads (two replicate rounds: R1/Dec 2023 and R2/May 2024), the North Dakota paired Healthy-Diseased/Barley Endos project on barley heads (with Nate Tyler and Grace Carey), and a comparison preparation of samples using HackFlex barcodes instead of the standard Illumina barcodes. Round 1 = R1, Round 2 = R2 for Tri5MB project.

```{r, results='hide', echo = FALSE}

colKeep <- c("Sample_ID", "I7_Index_ID", "I5_Index_ID", "Kingdom", "Chamber.Rep", "Strain", "Rep")

ps_r2_b@sam_data <- ps_r2_b@sam_data[,colKeep]
ps_r1_f@sam_data <- ps_r1_f@sam_data[,colKeep]
ps_r2_f@sam_data <- ps_r2_f@sam_data[,colKeep]


# make sequences the names of the ps objects
dna_r1_b <- data.frame(name = names(ps_r1_b@refseq), seq = unname(as.character(ps_r1_b@refseq)))
taxa_names(ps_r1_b) <- dna_r1_b$seq[ match(taxa_names(ps_r1_b), dna_r1_b$name) ]
dna_r2_b <- data.frame(name = names(ps_r2_b@refseq), seq = unname(as.character(ps_r2_b@refseq)))
taxa_names(ps_r2_b) <- dna_r2_b$seq[ match(taxa_names(ps_r2_b), dna_r2_b$name) ]
dna_r1_f <- data.frame(name = names(ps_r1_f@refseq), seq = unname(as.character(ps_r1_f@refseq)))
taxa_names(ps_r1_f) <- dna_r1_f$seq[ match(taxa_names(ps_r1_f), dna_r1_f$name) ]
dna_r2_f <- data.frame(name = names(ps_r2_f@refseq), seq = unname(as.character(ps_r2_f@refseq)))
taxa_names(ps_r2_f) <- dna_r2_f$seq[ match(taxa_names(ps_r2_f), dna_r2_f$name) ]

ps_f0 <- merge_phyloseq(ps_r1_f, ps_r2_f) 

## bacteria
#reorder taxa by abundance
abunOrder <- names(sort(colSums(ps_b0@otu_table), decreasing = TRUE))
abundances <- unname(sort(colSums(ps_b0@otu_table), decreasing = TRUE))
ps_b0@otu_table <- ps_b0@otu_table[, abunOrder]
ps_b0@tax_table <- ps_b0@tax_table[abunOrder, ]
ps_b0@refseq <- ps_b0@refseq[names(ps_b0@refseq)[match(abunOrder, names(ps_b0@refseq))] ]
#rename taxa
```

# Taxonomic Classification 

### FUNGI
* Qiime2 implementation of a Naive Bayesian Classifier using 
    * the UNITE, 2025.02 release, Euks, RefS, dynamic as the database (command line)
    * the SILVA, v.138.1, 99% species database
* Code for training Fungi database in ./code/qiime_featureclassifier_commandLine.txt

* Domain: Unassigned: 10,898 ASVs
* surprisingly, this is only 0.16% of the read count though.
* also manually removed all the NAs that were written in

```{r, results = 'hide'}
#write.csv(tax_table(ps_b_assn0b), "./data/R1R2Bact_combineSeqs_qiimeSilva-edit2.csv")
qiime.silva <- read.csv("./data/R1R2Bact_combineSeqs_qiimeSilva-edit2.csv",
                        stringsAsFactors = TRUE, row.names=1)

dim(qiime.silva %>% filter(grepl('Mitochondria', genus)))[1]
dim(qiime.silva %>% filter(grepl('Chloroplast', genus)))[1]
dim(qiime.silva %>% filter(grepl('Eukaryota', domain)))[1]
dim(qiime.silva %>% filter(grepl('remove-AphidSymbiont', remove)))[1]


#save PS again with tax table
rownames(qiime.silva) <- qiime.silva$X.1
qiime.silva %>% select(-X.1, -remove, -notes) -> qiime.silva
ps_b_assn0c <- ps_b_assn0b
ps_b_assn0c@tax_table <- tax_table(as.matrix(qiime.silva))
ps_b_assn0c
# Remove problematic taxa
ps_b_assn0d <- subset_taxa(ps_b_assn0c, genus != 'Mitochondria' & genus != "Chloroplast")
#sum(rowSums(ps_b_assn0d@otu_table))/sum(rowSums(ps_b_assn0c@otu_table))*100  
ps_b_assn0e <- subset_taxa(ps_b_assn0d, domain != "Eukaryota")
ps_b_assn <- subset_taxa(ps_b_assn0e, genus != "Buchnera" & 
        genus != "Wolbachia" & genus != "Rickettsia" & genus != "Spiroplasma")
## save out file
#save(ps_b_assn, file="./data/R1R2Bact_ps_b_assn.RData")
load("./data/R1R2Bact_ps_b_assn.RData")
ps_b_assn
```

* Genus: Mitochondria: 1,368 ASVs, 30.27% of the remaining data
* Genus: Chloroplast:    623 ASVs, 39.3% of the remaining data
* Domain: Eukaryota:   1,484 ASVs,  0.03% of the remaining data
* Likely Aphid Symbionts: 38 ASVs (obligate = Buchnera; facultative=Wolbachia, Ricksettia, Spiroplasma)
* 918 ASVs NA at phylum level, but Bact or Archaea at domain level. Leaving in, for now - no reason to remove them.


# Unmerge respective Bact and Fung datasets (hidden)

```{r, include = FALSE}
# table(sample_names(ps_b_assn) %in% sample_names(ps_r1_b))
# table(sample_names(ps_b_assn) %in% sample_names(ps_r2_b))
# 
# table(sample_names(ps_f_assn) %in% sample_names(ps_r1_f))
# table(sample_names(ps_f_assn) %in% sample_names(ps_r2_f))

ps_r1_b_assn <- subset_samples(ps_b_assn, sample_names(ps_b_assn) %in% sample_names(ps_r1_b))
ps_r1_b_assn <- filter_taxa(ps_r1_b_assn, function(x) mean(x) > 0, TRUE )
ps_r1_b_assn
ps_r2_b_assn <- subset_samples(ps_b_assn, sample_names(ps_b_assn) %in% sample_names(ps_r2_b))
ps_r2_b_assn <- filter_taxa(ps_r2_b_assn, function(x) mean(x) > 0, TRUE )
ps_r2_b_assn

ps_r1_f_assn <- subset_samples(ps_f_assn, sample_names(ps_f_assn) %in% sample_names(ps_r1_f))
ps_r1_f_assn <- filter_taxa(ps_r1_f_assn, function(x) mean(x) > 0, TRUE )
ps_r1_f_assn
ps_r2_f_assn <- subset_samples(ps_f_assn, sample_names(ps_f_assn) %in% sample_names(ps_r2_f))
ps_r2_f_assn <- filter_taxa(ps_r2_f_assn, function(x) mean(x) > 0, TRUE )
ps_r2_f_assn

```

* Bact: r1 dropped from 428 to 141 ASVs, r2 dropped from 16171 to 1885 ASVs
* Fung: r1 dropped from 66 to 60 ASVs, r2 dropped from 4007 to 3084 ASVs

# Controls

### Overview
```{r}
# define control samples
cont_name <- c("B-BactMock", "B-PCR1Blk", "B-PCR2Blk",
               "BactMock", "BactPCR1Blk", "BactPCR2Blk",   "BactMockHF", "B-HFPCR1Blk", 
                    #"HFPCR2Blk (this sample appears in both B & F R2 datasets)
               "F-FunMock", #two PCR blanks dropped out during DADA2
               "FunMock", "FunPCR1Blk", "FunPCR2Blk",       "FunMockHF", "HFPCR2Blk")

## examine controls
cont_r1_b <- subset_samples(ps_r1_b_assn, sample_names(ps_r1_b_assn) %in% cont_name)
cont_r1_b <- filter_taxa(cont_r1_b, function(x) mean(x) > 0, TRUE )
rowSums(cont_r1_b@otu_table)
#colSums(cont_r1_b@otu_table) #bASV34 + 325 are in mock, but ASV3 1 read in PCR2 blank

cont_r1_f <- subset_samples(ps_r1_f_assn, sample_names(ps_r1_f_assn) %in% cont_name)
cont_r1_f <- filter_taxa(cont_r1_f, function(x) mean(x) > 0, TRUE )
rowSums(cont_r1_f@otu_table)
#colSums(cont_r1_f@otu_table) #24 fungal ASVs in mock


cont_r2_b <- subset_samples(ps_r2_b_assn, sample_names(ps_r2_b_assn) %in% cont_name)
cont_r2_b <- filter_taxa(cont_r2_b, function(x) mean(x) > 0, TRUE )
rowSums(cont_r2_b@otu_table) # mocks both have > 100,000 reads, Blanks have 21-276 reads. 
    # HFPCRBlk only contam was Chloroplast/Mitochondria which were removed above
#colSums(cont_r2_b@otu_table) 
# cont_r2_b@otu_table['BactMock',]   # 22 bacterial ASVs in mock
# cont_r2_b@otu_table['BactMockHF',] # 32 bacterial ASVs in mock
# cont_r2_b@otu_table['BactPCR1Blk',] #bASV3 bASV4 bASV173 bASV183 bASV198 bASV233 bASV3127
# cont_r2_b@otu_table['BactPCR2Blk',] #bASV3
# cont_r2_b@otu_table['B-HFPCR1Blk',] #bASV3 bASV4 bASV173 bASV183 bASV198 bASV233 bASV3127 bASV4626

cont_r2_f <- subset_samples(ps_r2_f_assn, sample_names(ps_r2_f_assn) %in% cont_name)
cont_r2_f <- filter_taxa(cont_r2_f, function(x) mean(x) > 0, TRUE )
rowSums(cont_r2_f@otu_table) # mocks have 100K to 1mil reads, Blanks have 22-336 reads. 
# cont_r2_f@otu_table['FunMock',]   # 34 fungal ASVs in mock
# cont_r2_f@otu_table['FunMockHF',] # 52 fungal ASVs in mock
# cont_r2_f@otu_table['FunPCR1Blk',] #fASV1 fASV2       fASV5 fASV7     fASV8 fASV17 fASV20
# cont_r2_f@otu_table['FunPCR2Blk',] #fASV1 fASV2 fASV3       fASV7      fASV10 fASV59
# cont_r2_f@otu_table['HFPCR2Blk',]  #            fASV3                 fASV9 
```

#### NEGATIVES SUMMARY
* R1 bact had only 1 read in PCR2 blank and 0 in PCR1 blank. So easiest is just to drop low abundance ASVs (1 read or less)
* R1 Fung had no contamination
* R2 bact and fung both had PCR blanks with contamination on par to real samples, so will require SCRuB or similar decontamination approach.
* Can compare Mocks in R2 bact and R1/R2 fung to real composition to get a sense for read clustering.


### R1 Negatives Bacteria & Fungi
* Bacteria - no ASVs with 1 read count (contam level in PCR2), so instead will subtract 1 read from everything, to account for the 1 read contam in PCR2 blank
* Fungi - don't need to do anything
```{r}
## Bacteria
#table(colSums(ps_r1_b_assn@otu_table)) 
ps_r1_b_curated <- ps_r1_b_assn     # rename for consistent naming

otu_matrix <- ps_r1_b_curated@otu_table@.Data
otu_matrix_sub <- ifelse(otu_matrix > 0, otu_matrix - 1, otu_matrix)
otu_table(ps_r1_b_curated) <- otu_table(otu_matrix_sub, taxa_are_rows = FALSE) 
# remove PCR blanks from dataset
#table(rowSums(ps_r1_b_curated@otu_table) >0 )
ps_r1_b_curated <- subset_samples(ps_r1_b_curated, 
    sample_names(ps_r1_b_curated) %nin% c("B-PCR1Blk", "B-PCR2Blk") )

# ps_r1_b_curated #73 samples remaining
ps_r1_f_curated <- ps_r1_f_assn    # rename for consistent naming
```

### R2 Negatives Bacteria
#### format
* notes for bacteria: can do plate-based/spatially-explicit SCRuB, but not for fungi
```{r, include = FALSE}
# split up the projects
tri5mb_b <- subset_samples(ps_r2_b_assn, project == "Tri5MB" | project == "control")
hf_b <- subset_samples(ps_r2_b_assn, project == "HackFlex" | project == "HackFlex-control")
# create meta/mat for scrub
meta_tri5 <- (as(sample_data(tri5mb_b), "data.frame"))
mat_tri5 <- (as(otu_table(tri5mb_b), "matrix"))
meta_hf <- (as(sample_data(hf_b), "data.frame"))
mat_hf <- (as(otu_table(hf_b), "matrix"))

# format for SCRuB
meta_tri5 <- meta_tri5 %>% arrange(sequenceCode) %>%
    mutate(sample_type = 
        if_else(controlName == "BactPCR1Blk", "BlankPCR1", 
                if_else(controlName == "BactPCR2Blk", "BlankPCR2", "other"))) %>%
    mutate(is_control = if_else(sample_type == "BlankPCR1" | sample_type == "BlankPCR2", 
            "TRUE", "FALSE")) %>%
    mutate(sample_well = well) %>%
    #mutate(sample_plate = plate) %>%
    select(is_control, sample_type, sample_well) #%>%      
meta_tri5$sample_well <- as.character(meta_tri5$sample_well)
meta_hf <- meta_hf %>% arrange(sequenceCode) %>%
    mutate(sample_type = 
        if_else(controlName == "B-HFPCR1Blk", "BlankPCR1", "other")) %>%   # HFPCR2Blk = 0 reads
    mutate(is_control = if_else(sample_type == "BlankPCR1", #| sample_type == "BlankPCR2", 
            "TRUE", "FALSE")) %>%
    mutate(sample_well = well) %>%
    #mutate(sample_plate = plate) %>%
    select(is_control, sample_type, sample_well) #%>%      
meta_hf$sample_well <- as.character(meta_hf$sample_well)

# remove HFPCR2Blk with 0 reads
meta_hf <- meta_hf[rownames(meta_hf) != "HFPCR2Blk",] 
mat_hf <- mat_hf[rownames(mat_hf) != "HFPCR2Blk",] 

# rearrange rows to match 
mat_tri5 %>% data.frame %>% mutate(ids = rownames(mat_tri5)) %>%
    arrange(ids) %>% select(-ids) %>% as.matrix -> mat_tri5
#identical(rownames(mat_tri5), rownames(meta_tri5)) #TRUE
mat_hf %>% data.frame %>% mutate(ids = rownames(mat_hf)) %>%
    arrange(ids) %>% select(-ids) %>% as.matrix -> mat_hf
#identical(rownames(mat_hf), rownames(meta_hf)) #TRUE
```

#### CURATION SUMMARY
* SCRuB decontamination removed a large number of taxa (likely low abundance) from all the R2 datasets. 34%-47% of taxa by count removed across all four R2 linked datasets.
* However, because of the way SCRuB accounts for sample depth overall in balancing read loss due to contamination, the total read loss was minimal, ranging from 0.12% - 1.05% across all four R2 linked datasets.
